notes.text: The leaf asks for a preliminary devissage theorem: a global signed topological groupoid, with its graph and sign functors and elementary operations, should be reconstructed from the displayed connected fixed-type groupoids and functors. The underlined marginal exception removes operations 4 and 5 from the initial range 1:7; the larger margin explicitly says the displayed information is not quite sufficient. This is a proposed programme, not a proof on this leaf.

The local definition sets nu equal to the number of boundary components and requires card(R intersect C_a)=1 for every boundary component. The figure carries the corresponding nu label and states weight 1 on its free edges. I checked this numerical agreement against the written definition. I did not establish the general graph construction or the reconstruction theorem.

The final sentence defines the unmarked fixed-type groupoid through triples (X,phi,phi) with X of type g,nu. The marginal category is written T_{g,infinity}; it is not silently changed to T_{g,nu} merely to match the main display. No definition of that infinity-indexed object is supplied on this page.

The first cancelled diagram has a rightward arrow to [plus-minus 1] and a downward arrow to Ens(nu). A separate lower cancelled T object has an oblique down-left arrow. Its crossed endpoint supplies no secure separate object. The old superscript, old horizontal-arrow label and isolated erased sign remain doubtful.

The live enclosure has top and bottom bars and a separate left side, with no right side. Its lower-left annotation is on siglera, joined by a curved leader; the leader is not replaced by an opening parenthesis and no closing parenthesis is supplied. The annotation has gnu without a comma.

Five rays are drawn in the small graph; the central one is faint. The brace-like mark is overworked and is reproduced by a path, not identified solely by a font brace. The numerical parameter remains nu: five drawn rays are a schematic count, not an assertion that nu=5. Under tilde-Sigma, the two short vertical strokes and partial-X form a vertical annotation column.

The small pale mark after que is above the word baseline and is weaker than the adjacent writing; it is not promoted to punctuation. The lower folio 61 is transcribed without attributing its different-looking hand to a named writer.
